To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the composition of species assemblages in Amazonia is mainly determined by environmental conditions, but that rivers and geographical distance also have an important effect.
the distribution of most animal and plant species in Amazonia is influenced by both environmental gradients and isolation by distance or by the Amazon River.

The wide and relatively ancient Amazon River tends to determine differences in the composition of most biological groups, although the effects of environment and geographic distance are generally more important than the effect of large rivers in explaining changes in species composition at broad scales in the Amazon basin.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the processes that structure the distribution of species across the Amazonian landscape and the role of rivers, environmental gradients, and geographic distance.
the role of environmental filtering in shaping the composition of communities in Amazonia.
understanding how species are distributed across space.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the relative importance of these processes varies according to biological group.
dispersal limitation (geographic distance and rivers) and environmental filtering are both important in shaping the turnover in species composition in Amazonia.
dispersal limitation and environmental filtering are both important processes that shape the distribution of species, but their relative importance varies among taxa.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Amazonian biota is strongly structured by environmental gradients and geographic distance.
environmental filtering, isolation by distance and dispersal limitation are important factors in shaping species distributions and community composition in Amazonian ecosystems.

“Environmental gradients and geographic distance are important determinants for community composition in Amazonian forests, but the relative contribution of each process varies among biological groups”.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the distribution of species and communities in Amazonia is influenced by both environmental gradients and dispersal limitation.
the relative importance of environmental filtering versus dispersal limitation in shaping the distribution of species varies across taxa.
the effects of environmental filtering and geographic distance on community assembly are pervasive in Amazonia.
